newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-GREENE UPSETS FAVOURITES IN WORLD 100 METRES FINAL.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GREENE UPSETS FAVOURITES IN WORLD 100 METRES FINAL.

text.p: American Maurice Greene upset favourites Ato Boldon and defending champion Donovan Bailey to win the world 100 metres title in 9.86 seconds on Sunday.
Only Bailey and fellow-American Leroy Burrell have ever run faster.
The 23-year-old American champion had predicted before the race that Bailey's world record of 9.84 seconds would fall.
He may have been wrong on that count but still did enough to win ahead of Canadian Bailey, the Olympic champion, and compatriot Tim Montgomery.
Bailey clocked 9.91 seconds with Montgomery recording 9.94.
Namibian Frankie Fredericks, the Olympic silver medallist, finished just one-hundredth of a second behind in fourth place.
Boldon, Greene's training partner, who clocked 9.87 seconds in the second round on Saturday had a bad start, was never in contention and finished fifth in 10.02 seconds.
Nigerian Davidson Ezinwa (10.10), Canadian Bruny Surin (10.12) and American Mike Marsh (10.29), who will be 30 on Monday, occupied the remaining positions.
Greene, who had run four successive 9.90s going into the final never looked like losing after his lightning start.

With Marion Jones winning the women's 100 metres, he completed the first U.S. double at either the Olympics or world championships since the 1988 Seoul Olympics when Carl Lewis and Florence Griffith Joyner won their respective titles.
